decisions.reason: The source establishes a component-cost policy for a future integrated-board redesign but does not change the existing task-local assistance for ordering the current boards.
Preference for JLCPCB Basic components may influence future component selection, but it does not alter the existing requirement that BOM entries be correct and assembly-ready.
The candidate concerns production files for the existing sensor board; the proposed integrated-board redesign does not cancel or modify that existing handoff requirement.
The integrated-board cost and component policy says nothing about KiCad library portability or project-file self-containment.
This candidate is explicitly scoped to the modular main board, while the source introduces a separate integrated-board redesign context and does not revise the existing modular layout.
The current mechanical constraints apply to the modular power board; the proposed integrated board is a separate redesign and does not modify those existing constraints.
Reducing cost while preserving functionality does not remove or change the AXP2101 thermal-pad requirement.
The source does not change the required DCDC1 voltage, compensation behavior, or regulated 3.3V rail.

The enclosure currently accommodates three boards, while the proposed redesign uses one integrated board; it is unclear whether the redesign supersedes this enclosure configuration or is a separate future variant.
The integrated-board proposal preserves functionality and does not specify any change to monitored rails, the monitoring IC, channels, or measurement coverage.
This candidate is scoped to the existing modular sensor board; the separate integrated-board redesign does not revise its current mechanical-layout state.
The cost-focused integrated-board decision does not change any ESP32-S3 GPIO assignment or compatibility constraint.
